### Week 13 Homework Instructions

- Set of 4 .csv files in data/homework.
- Each file is a time series of temperature and light data collected in tide pools in Oregon by Jenn Fields.
  - Bring in all 4 files and calculate the **mean** and **standard deviation** of both temperature (`Temp.C`) and light (`Intensity.lux`) for each tide pool.
  - Use `for loop` and `map()` functions in script

```{r Load Libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(wesanderson)
```

## Reading in the Data

- Files have a `PoolID` column, so we can group by that column, rather than the filename
- Four tide pools in Oregon, logged every \~15 minutes from 16 June to 17 August 2019.
- Each file holds one pool, identified by a `PoolID` column, with two *Phyllospadix* removal pools and two controls

```{r Reading in Data}
#| label: list-files


## Let's get to the folder
PoolPath <- here("Week_13", "Data", "homework")

## full.names = TRUE keeps the whole path, which is what
## read_csv() needs to actually open them.
files <- dir(path = PoolPath, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
files

## Inspect one before building anything
glimpse(read_csv(files[1]))
```


- After first inspection:
  - `Intensity.lux` records values above 1000 with a comma ("1,003"), so the column reads as character
  - `as.numeric()` would turn every bright reading into NA
  - As such we need use `col_number()`, which strips grouping marks at read time

### Method 1: for loop

1.  Pre-allocate an empty tibble with one row per file
2.  Loop over `seq_along(files)`, reading each file
3.  Assign each result into row \[i\]

```{r}
#| label: for-loop
#| message: false

# Pre-allocate: one row per file, one column per value to compute
# Growing a data frame inside a loop re-copies the whole thing every
# Iteration, so it gets slower (allocating first avoids)

loop_summary <- tibble(
  PoolID     = rep(NA, length(files)),
  treatment  = rep(NA, length(files)),
  mean_temp  = rep(NA, length(files)),
  sd_temp    = rep(NA, length(files)),
  mean_light = rep(NA, length(files)),
  sd_light   = rep(NA, length(files))
)

# seq_along(files) rather than 1:length(files). 
# If files were empty, 1:length(files) is 1:0, so the loop would run twice on nothing
# seq_along() returns an empty sequence and the loop correctly does nothing.

for (i in seq_along(files)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(
    files[i],
    col_types = cols(Intensity.lux = col_number()),  # the comma fix
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

# PoolID comes from the data rather than the filename
  
  loop_summary$PoolID[i]     <- raw_data$PoolID[1]
  loop_summary$treatment[i]  <- raw_data$Removal_Control[1]

# na.rm = TRUE throughout: Temp.C has blank cells
# (10 in TP1, 25 in TP4)
# A single NA without this makes the whole mean NA
  
  loop_summary$mean_temp[i]  <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  loop_summary$sd_temp[i]    <- sd(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE)
  loop_summary$mean_light[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
  loop_summary$sd_light[i]   <- sd(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE)
}

loop_summary
```

### Method 2: purrr `map()`

1.  `set_names()` so each file path labels its list element
2.  `map(read_csv)` to make a list of four tibbles
3.  `list_rbind()` fills data frame, then `group_by()` + `summarise()`

```{r}
#| label: purrr-map
#| message: false

map_summary <- files |>
# set_names() labels each list element with its file path
# list_rbind() makes labels into a column 
  
  set_names() |>

# map() applies read_csv() to each path and returns a list of 4 tibbles
# The function is wrapped so col_types can be passed
  map(\(f) read_csv(f,
                    col_types = cols(Intensity.lux = col_number()),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)) |>

# list_rbind() stacks the list into one data frame names_to records which file each row came from 
# (map_dfr() does the same but is superseded.)
  
  list_rbind(names_to = "filepath") |>

# Grouping on PoolID rather than filepath
# Foundation_spp and Removal_Control are constant
# group_by() simply carries them into the output
  
  group_by(PoolID, Foundation_spp, Removal_Control) |>
  summarise(
    mean_temp  = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_temp    = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_light = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_light   = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

map_summary
```

### Method 3: `read_csv()` with a vector of paths

```{r}
#| label: read-csv-vector
#| message: false

# Since readr 2.0, read_csv() accepts a vector of file paths and stacks them
tidepool_summary <- read_csv(
    files,
    id = "filepath",
    col_types = cols(Intensity.lux = col_number())
  ) |>
# col_number() strips grouping marks, so "1,003" parses as 1003 instead of becoming NA
# Avoids dropping every reading >= 1000 
  
  group_by(PoolID, Foundation_spp, Removal_Control) |>

  summarise(
    mean_temp  = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_temp    = sd(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_light = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_light   = sd(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_temp     = sum(!is.na(Temp.C)),      
# how many readings each mean rests on
    n_light    = sum(!is.na(Intensity.lux)),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

tidepool_summary
```

## Do all methods agree?

```{r}
#| label: verify

## If any method handled the comma separators differently, the light means would diverge by an order of magnitude

all.equal(loop_summary |> 
            select(mean_temp, sd_temp, mean_light, sd_light) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |> arrange(mean_temp),
    map_summary |> 
      ungroup() |>
      select(mean_temp, sd_temp, mean_light, sd_light) |>
      arrange(mean_temp),
    check.attributes = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tidepool
#| tbl-cap: "Mean and standard deviation of temperature and light in four Oregon tide pools, June–August 2019."

tidepool_summary |>
  select(
    "Pool"          = PoolID,
    "Treatment"     = Removal_Control,
    "Mean temp (°C)" = mean_temp,
    "SD temp"       = sd_temp,
    "Mean light (lux)" = mean_light,
    "SD light"      = sd_light
  ) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_minimal("hover") |>
  column_spec(3, background = wes_palette("GrandBudapest1")[1]) |>
  column_spec(5, background = wes_palette("GrandBudapest1")[4])

```

@tbl-tidepool summarizes how temperature is near-identical across pools (13.1–13.3 °C, SD ≈ 2.3), while light differs roughly tenfold between treatments.

Removing the canopy changed the light environment and left the thermal environment largely unchanged.
